title: Identity, LDAP personality and persistence boundaries
rules: The neutral Identity Directory owns semantic identity; LDAP is a protocol/personality edge.
oorexxEntityId is platform semantic identity; entryUUID is LDAP entry identity. They are intentionally distinct.
A DN is a directory address and may change without changing semantic identity.
Vendor LDAP personalities translate external vocabulary at the edge and cannot silently redefine identity, authority, credential or key-lifetime semantics.
Credential persistence contains secretRef, never raw secret values.
DirectoryStore persists accepted DirectoryChange facts but cannot reinterpret LDAP schema or authority policy.
The durable commit boundary is write-before-memory: failed durable append must not advance in-memory revision or entity state.
One semantic DirectoryChange produces one peer-update request identity independent of target count or carrier path.
Duplicate changeId with divergent semantic identity fails closed.
Replication is idempotent durable distribution, not consensus.
